notes:
Summary: SlateBeam builds an in-IDE copilot focused on single-keystroke responsiveness for completions and inline refactors. Primary goal: deliver a best-in-class editor UX by minimizing TTFT (time-to-first-token), smoothing jitter, and enabling token-budget controls so engineers never see long stalls or mid-completion truncations. They are in an evaluation POC—internal engineering heavy, product-led demo for leadership.

Requirements & acceptance criteria (customer-provided):
- TTFT target: median <= 50ms for local dev editors and <= 80ms over VPC peered hosts; p99 under 250ms.
- Jitter: desirable jitter band < 20ms for median workloads; spikes tolerated but must be explainable.
- Streaming behavior: support sub-token streaming/chunked frames so the editor can render partial suggestions and apply incremental edits.
- Backpressure semantics: editor must be able to pause/resume streams and request aborts without leaving the assistant in an inconsistent state.
- Token budget tuning: want server-side per-session budgets with graceful truncation and soft warnings to client-side (editor) to show 'partial suggestion — expand?' UI.
- Model pinning & fallbacks: pin to a deterministic 13B quantized variant for primary completions; fallback to a cheaper 6B variant with clear quality signal and heuristic-based routing under overload.
- Security: VPC private endpoints, SAML SSO for admin console, KMS integration for key management, and audit logs for token-level requests.

POC work so far / timeline:
- 2025-11-10: Intro demo (Ethan + Nina) — product team liked streaming primitives and prefix caching idea.
- 2025-11-17: Technical deep-dive w/ engs (CTO present) — shared synthetic editor workload (see Drive).
- 2025-11-25: Baseline run on Redwood hosted API using our harness: median TTFT 120ms, p95 420ms, jitter wide (spikes to 900ms under concurrent sessions) — unacceptable for interactive UX.
- 2025-12-03: Optimize session config from Redwood Optimize suggestions (smaller batch windows, KV caching enabled) — median TTFT down to ~68ms but p95 still ~300ms; observed partial improvements in jitter.
- 2025-12-08: Security questionnaire returned; legal flagged data retention and DPA language.
- 2025-12-10: Sync w/ Redwood SE (Nina) to scope Dedicated POC and gather price/commit options.

Technical notes from engineering:
- Editor workload specifics: ~35 concurrent active sessions per dev pool, average completion length 20-60 tokens, occasional 200+ token refactors. Key metric is fast first-byte (visual), then sustained token throughput for longer completions.
- Batching policy tension: batching helps throughput but adds latency; need fine-grained continuous batching limits (max batch wait < 12ms for interactive path).
- Cache strategy: prefix/KV caching for common completion prefixes reduces token compute by ~30% in baseline runs. Cache misses cause worst-case TTFT spikes.
- Backpressure behavior: current editor expects immediate ACK on abort; need API-level abort semantics + traceable event.

Quote from CTO (paraphrase): 'If we can't make suggestions feel instantaneous, the copilot won't be adopted — even if raw quality is better. We need predictable latency above all.'

Next steps (agreed):
1) Redwood to spin up Dedicated POC with pinned 13B quantized model and pre-configured continuous batching policy (ETA 2025-12-18).
2) SlateBeam to run 48-hour scripted editor run (provided harness) and deliver telemetry (TTFT, p50/p95/p99, jitter histogram, token throughput).
3) Agreement on SLO doc: define pass/fail gates (median TTFT, p95, abort semantics).
4) Legal to finalize DPA & data residency clause — target sign by 2026-01-15.

Open risks / blockers:
- Internal procurement cycle (needs VP Eng approval) — timeline uncertain.
- DPA retention language — slatebeam requires 90-day log retention and retention controls in UI.
- SAML exchange timing — their IdP is on a locked change window (next maintenance: 2026-01-03).

Stubs / links: POC harness repo (drive link above), Fireflies calls ff-8347/ff-8421 contain raw demo recordings, Jira INF-4123 for initial integration issue where streaming abort dropped state.

Notes style: shorthand + action-oriented; product and eng priorities emphasized.
